title: Vocabulary Quiz — Unit 9A: Shopping and prices
subtitle: Shops, the shopping centre and money

words.def: a shop where you buy medicine
words.sent: I’m going to the ___ to buy some aspirin.

words.def: a shop that sells books
words.sent: I bought two novels in the ___.

words.def: a big shop with many different things on different floors
words.sent: You can buy clothes, shoes and furniture in a ___.

words.def: a shop that sells things to wear
words.sent: My son needs new jeans, so we’re going to a ___.

words.def: a place where you can quickly get a burger and chips
words.sent: We had a burger at the ___ before the film.

words.def: a place where you drink coffee and eat cakes
words.sent: Let’s sit in the ___ and have a coffee.

words.def: a place where buses stop and people wait
words.sent: I’m waiting at the ___ for the number 5.

words.def: the way into a building
words.sent: Let’s meet at the main ___ of the shopping centre.

words.def: a place where you leave your car
words.sent: I left my car in the ___ next to the shopping centre.

words.def: a place where you can ask questions in a big building
words.sent: Ask at the ___ if you can’t find the shop.

words.def: steps that go up and down inside a building
words.sent: The lift isn’t working, so we’re taking the ___.

words.def: a machine where you take money out of your bank account
words.sent: I need some money. Is there a ___ near here?

words.def: things like tables, chairs and sofas
words.sent: We’re buying new ___ for the living room.

words.def: something you take when you are ill
words.sent: I’ve got a headache. I need some ___.

words.def: money in coins and notes, not by card
words.sent: Do you take cards or only ___?

words.def: the money used in the UK
words.sent: In London the T-shirt costs ten ___s.

words.def: the money used in many countries in Europe
words.sent: In Paris I paid in ___s.

words.def: the money used in the USA
words.sent: In New York the coffee costs three ___s.

words.def: a small coin; one hundredth of a dollar or euro
words.sent: A dollar is one hundred ___s.

words.def: a piece of paper that lets you go into a cinema or on a train
words.sent: I just bought our ___s for the film.
